Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together an initial pricing package for LedgerWorks: 

Recap (from our call):
- Primary use: document understanding and automated reconciliation for payments/fraud ops.
- Expected traffic: ~1.5M to 4M tokens/day initially, ramp to ~12M tokens/day in 12 months (peak).
- Environments: Prod + Staging; possibly a sandbox for partners (so 2-3 environments).
- Data controls: VPC/private deployment required; SOC 2 + enterprise KMS.
- Procurement timeline: Q2 evaluation, decision in June.

Open items for pricing:
1) Can you confirm the delta between typical and peak token volumes (you mentioned spikes)?
2) Do you have a target unit economics (e.g., target $/1M tokens) or budget band we should aim at?
3) Confirm number of environments that need dedicated capacity / licensing (prod/staging/sandbox).

Next steps: I attached a short pricing summary and a token-volume worksheet - if you can populate the green column with realistic monthly averages/peaks, Marissa (cc'd) will use that to build a Private/VPC licensing + reserved capacity recommendation.

Ben -

Thanks for the summary. A few answers inline and one ask: please put together an initial estimate we can show procurement.

- Volumes: Our current conservative estimate is ~2M tokens/day (avg) with spikes to ~6M tokens/day. The roadmap is to hit ~10-12M/day in 9-12 months if pilot goes well.
- Spikes: spiky traffic primarily during batch reconciliation jobs (nightly) and after product releases.
- Environments: we definitely need Prod and Staging on dedicated capacity. Sandbox for partners is optional but preferred. So count 2 guaranteed, 1 optional.
- Budget target: we haven't nailed a target $/1M tokens. Procurement gave a rough band of $60k-$80k/month total for this initiative (including software + support) for year 1.

Question: Can you explain how Redwood's Private licensing is structured? Specifically:
1) One-time license vs. annual subscription?
2) Are licenses per environment, per cluster, or per-node?
3) How do you handle reserved capacity + burst to hosted (if needed) - is there a per-token overage?

Appreciate if Marissa can include a pricing scenario that maps to the $60k-$80k/month band you see above.

Thanks —
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing discovery & token volumes - LedgerWorks

Hi Alex / Priya -

Great to meet you both on the call. Quick dot-point answers and an attached term sheet with example scenarios.

Licensing model (Private / VPC):
- Structure: Annual subscription model (preferred for private installs) + optional one-time onboarding fee.
- Unit: License is per-environment seat (an "environment" maps to a logically isolated deployment: Prod, Staging, Sandbox). Customers typically buy 2 environments for Prod+Staging; sandbox is optional and discounted if purchased together.
- Capacity: Reserved GPU capacity billed monthly as part of the subscription (committed throughput tiers). We include a burst policy that can route overflow to hosted capacity; overflow is billed per 1M tokens at a separate overage rate.

Typical cost levers:
- Base subscription (per-environment) - covers runtime license, basic support (business hours), security integrations.
- Reserved capacity (GPU pool) - tiered by committed token throughput; higher tiers lower the $/1M effective unit cost.
- Support tier add-on - Standard, Premium, Enterprise (Premium includes 4hr response for Sev1, Enterprise 1hr + dedicated TAM).
- Overages / hosted fallback - per-1M token rate for burst beyond reserved capacity.

Example scenarios (high level) - see attached license_term_sheet.pdf for numbers:
- Scenario A (cost-conservative): 2 envs (Prod+Staging), reserved tier for 4M/day avg (~120M/month), burst to hosted for peaks. Estimated annual subscription + reserved = ~$650k/year (~$54k/month) + overage buffer. Effective unit cost target: ~$45-$55 per 1M tokens depending on burst mix.
- Scenario B (performance-focused): 3 envs (Prod+Staging+Sandbox), reserved for 8M/day avg (~240M/month) with higher reserved buffer. Estimated = ~$1.0M/year (~$83k/month). Effective unit cost: ~$30-$40 per 1M tokens at this committed volume.

Mapping to your $60k-$80k/month band: Scenario A is in range if you stay nearer the low end of the spike profile and keep sandbox optional. Scenario B pushes toward the top of your band but provides lower $/1M. We'll size exact GPU/reserved tiers after you fill the token workbook.

Support tiers we recommend for LedgerWorks given production SLAs: Premium (4hr Sev1) or Enterprise (1hr + TAM). We can include the support pricing as an add-on line in the quote; Enterprise is usually selected where on-call ops depend on low-latency inference.

Attachments: license_term_sheet.pdf

Next steps: Ben / I will take the completed token workbook and build 2 tailored options (Conservative & Performance) with line-item pricing (license, reserved capacity, support, expected overage). Can you confirm: final signoff owner (procurement) and an internal target decision date?

- Marissa
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
